text.p: Western Pacific Airlines Inc said Monday that it would acquire Frontier Airlines Inc, exchanging 0.75 shares of Western stock for each share of Frontier.
The companies said both their boards' had approved a definitive agreement on the pact, which they said would give Frontier stockholders about 31 percent ownership in a combined company.

In a joint statement, the companies said that three Frontier directors would join the Western Pacific board, which would be expanded to nine members. Spokesmen for the companies could not be immediately reached Monday evening for further comment.
They said they had targeted August 1 to begin an interim code share arrangement. The arrangement would offer 76 daily jet departures from Denver International serving 25 markets.
The companies said by year's end, they plan to have 86 daily departures serving 26 markets and raise the number of Boeing 737 aircraft they operate to 34 from 30.
Western Pacific shares closed Monday up 1/8 at 5-1/2. Frontier shares closed down 1/8 at 3-7/8.

"This is an exciting combination that makes great sense for both companies. In addition to helping us reach a critical mass, combining the carriers will allow us to offer a significant number of flights in each market," Western Pacific said in the statement.
